purpose: Target-specific, machine-governed dispositions for container-image vulnerability findings. Replaces the bare global .trivyignore, whose entries were CVE IDs with prose governance: a bare ID suppresses that CVE EVERYWHERE, in every image and every package, so it could silently hide a genuinely new occurrence of the same CVE in a different component.
enforcement_model: The gate scans with NO suppression (--ignorefile /dev/null) to obtain the complete finding set, then reconciles that set against the records below. An unmatched finding fails the gate. A record that matches nothing fails the gate as unused. Trivy's own ignore mechanism is never relied upon, so suppression cannot happen without a matching governed record.

records.reason: c-ares 1.34.6-r0 is an OS package in postgres:18-alpine. The fix (1.34.8-r0) is not present in any published postgres:18-alpine build, so no patched official image exists to re-pin to. The finding is DoS-class against DNS resolution.
compensating_controls: PostgreSQL is bound to 127.0.0.1 only (docker-compose.yml publishes 127.0.0.1:5432:5432), so the resolver is not reachable from off-host.
Phase 0 is a LOCAL-ONLY development profile under EXC-P0-004; external or customer-data use is prohibited.
ADR-P0-01 monthly patch cadence re-pins and re-scans as a blocking release gate.

records.reason: Go standard-library CVEs compiled into the upstream gosu 1.19 binary shipped by EVERY current official postgres image variant. gosu executes once at container start to drop root privileges and then exits; the affected surfaces (net/http, net/mail, crypto DoS classes) are not exercised by that use. No patched official postgres build exists.
compensating_controls: gosu runs once at container start and is not a long-lived process or network listener.
Phase 0 is a LOCAL-ONLY development profile under EXC-P0-004.
ADR-P0-01 monthly patch cadence re-pins and re-scans as a blocking release gate.
